title: Strengthening SONC relaxations with constraints derived from variable bounds
contribution: Even-power constraints derived from finite variable bounds give the SONC Lagrangian a simplex cover of monomial squares (Theorem 6), raising finite root SONC bounds from 9 to 330 of 349 instances, and an experimental SCIP relaxator shows SONC bounds not yet competitive with LP bounds (better on 6 instances, about 4.9 times the time).
problem_entry: A relaxation inside branch and bound must improve with node bounds, but plain bound terms do not help a SONC bound (x_i is not a monomial square) and most Lagrangians lack even vertices, so standard SONC gives a finite root bound on only 9 of 349 instances (abstract; pp. 2–3, 10, 16).
key_idea: Add x_i^α ≤ max{|l_i|, |u_i|}^α with even α large enough (Theorem 6) that the new exponents and the origin cover every non-square term; degree costs SONC nothing, so structure is bought with degree; the Dressler–Iliman–de Wolff Lagrangian GP relaxation is left unchanged (pp. 6–12, 14).
assumptions: Continuous polynomial programs over Rⁿ with finite bounds on every variable; ST-polynomial Lagrangian, no monomial-square inner terms, one strictly positive term per vertex coefficient (Theorem 5); relaxation used only if at least half the constraints are polynomial; data: the RAPOSa set, 180 Dalkiran–Sherali random and 169 MINLPLib polynomial instances (pp. 3, 8–10, 13, 15).
proof_devices: Explicit barycentric coordinates as the witness of a cover: β_i/α_ii on the new axis exponents, the remainder on the origin, nonnegative by the exponent bound α_ii ≥ (n + (n mod 2)) · max ‖β‖∞ (Theorem 6 and proof, pp. 11–12)
Evenness by construction: the factor n + (n mod 2) is even, so the new exponents are monomial squares (p. 11)
Validity by monotonicity: dropping monomial-square inner terms or monomial-square vertices can only lower the bound (pp. 8, 14)
Restated relaxation chain f0 − γSONC ≤ f0 − γ* ≤ f* for the Lagrangian GP (Theorems 4–5, pp. 8–9)
Plug-in design: undo SCIP's objective-variable reformulation; only in-support bound constraints if the Lagrangian is ST, Theorem 6 exponents and discarded vertices otherwise (pp. 13–15)
The step from a cover to a finite bound is not written as a separate statement (my reading of pp. 10–12)
experiments: Development SCIP only, three arms (standard SONC; SONC plus bound constraints with three exponent choices; default SCIP), 349 instances, 3600 s, gap 0.01%, Xeon E5-2660 2.60 GHz with 128 GB per node, threads not stated, no seeds or permutations; root status census (finite bounds 9 → 330), shifted geometric means (time shift 1 s, nodes shift 100; Table 3 states no shift), best-time rule t/t1 ≤ 1.01 and t/t2 ≤ 0.9, root-bound wins (LP 305, SONC 6, equal 38) and gap closed; time 25.29 → 123.04 s, nodes 27.04 → 34.60; failures printed; exponent default chosen on the same set; call rule described two ways (every 10 nodes, p. 13; depths that are multiples of 10, p. 15) (pp. 13, 15–19).
positioning: Between spatial branch and bound with RLT (RAPOSa) and certificate hierarchies (SOS: Shor, Nesterov, Lasserre, Parrilo; SONC: Iliman and de Wolff; SAGE: Chandrasekaran and Shah), continuing Seidler's SONC branch and bound; §§2–3 summarize known theory; RAPOSa's test set is used but RAPOSa is not run (pp. 2–3, 6, 15).
writing: Headline as a count in the abstract (9 → 330 of 349); the negative result announced in the introduction before any table (p. 3); contributions as (i) and (ii) (p. 2); causes hedged ('This might have been caused', p. 16; 'most likely', p. 19).
limits_future: Not competitive with default LP relaxations (25.29 → 123.04 s; LP root bound better on 305 instances, SONC on 6), put down to SONC cost, no warm start and no SONC-aware presolve, reductions or branching; 4 infeasibility detections lost; discarded vertices weaken bounds; five of the six root gains are one-variable unconstrained instances (my reading of Table 5); the headline 330 uses an exponent outside Theorem 6 in general (choices within it: 308 and 314); future: a SONC-based branch and bound with SONC-aware reductions and branching, better use of bounds and constraints; remaining data not yet public (pp. 14, 16–20).

method_links.note: steps 1, 5 and 7: gaps printed where they arise with counts and suspected causes (4 lost infeasibility detections, 12 extra timeouts; slowdown and 6 against 305 root-bound wins with named causes; multiplier consistency across ST pieces left open); the lost comparison read as the next design, a SONC-aware branch and bound

step 2 argued, not measured: the gap is put down to the years of integration LP relaxations have had, with no like-for-like run; step 6 not reached: the relaxator stays on a PySCIPOpt development branch; the skill's trajectory notes find no journal version (06-trajectory.md §6, item 4)

component off and on inside one development SCIP with default SCIP printed; slowdown read from the pair of factors, time about 4.9 against nodes about 1.3 (my arithmetic); a predecessor's test set reused (RAPOSa's, step 7), but no rival solver run and no harder set added

scope: no exact arithmetic or safe rounding; the SONC bound comes from a floating-point conic solve (POEM, CVXPY, ECOS) and replaces the LP bound when larger; numerical trouble visible only where a solve fails, avoided by small exponents; no independent check of the bound (Method 4 not applied); consistent with the Method 5 limitation that repair for cone constraints is untested in his work

new_pattern_candidates.pattern: theorem's safe choice vs measured default
new_pattern_candidates.evidence: Theorem 6 guarantees a cover for exponents of at least (n + (n mod 2)) · max ‖β‖∞; the default 2 · max β_i + 4 leaves the theorem in general for larger n to keep degrees and numerics small, is said to lie outside it, and covers every instance of the set; the choices within the theorem give 308 and 314 finite bounds against 330

new_pattern_candidates.pattern: make an imported relaxation bound-aware before embedding it in branch and bound
new_pattern_candidates.evidence: plain bound constraints add nothing to a SONC bound because x_i is not a monomial square; even-power bound constraints let the relaxation use tighter node bounds, which the paper names as the requirement for a relaxation solved inside branch and bound

new_pattern_candidates.pattern: default chosen on the evaluation set (negative)
new_pattern_candidates.evidence: the exponent default A(4) is chosen by comparing three variants on the same 349 instances that carry the headline 9 → 330; the variants within Theorem 6 give 308 and 314

transferable: (D4) Give an imported relaxation the structure it needs through redundant constraints derived from variable bounds: x_i^α ≤ max{|l_i|, |u_i|}^α with even α adds one monomial square per variable and tightens by itself as branching shrinks the box (pp. 2, 10–11)

(D4) Prove a covering condition by writing the witness: barycentric weights β_i/α_ii on the axis exponents, the remainder on the origin, and an exponent bound chosen so that the remainder is nonnegative (Theorem 6, pp. 11–12)

(D4) Check what the host solver's own reformulations do to a plug-in's structural requirement and undo them inside the plug-in: SCIP's objective variable is removed and its constraint moved back into the objective (p. 14)
(D5) Report a new relaxation first as a census of root termination statuses per arm (optimal, infeasible, unsolvable, interrupted, did not run), then speed (Tables 1–2, pp. 15–17)
(D5) Read a slowdown against the node count: a time factor far above the node factor puts the cost in each node, not in a larger search (Table 4, p. 18)

(D5) When the theorem's parameter is numerically fragile, run the guaranteed choice, a padded one and a cheap unguaranteed one side by side, report statuses for each, and say which one lies outside the theorem (Table 2, p. 17)
coauthors: Ksenia Bestuzheva (first author, ZIB), Helena Völker (ZIB)

quotes.text: Overall, SONC relaxations are currently not competitive with the LP relaxations employed by default.
Although this choice does not satisfy the conditions of Theorem 6 and thus does not in general guarantee a valid cover, it is independent of n and leads to a much smaller increase in the degree.
